feedback_interpretation: The authoritative state is 813 observed records and 2,517 candidates. H15 is weakened: m75's repeated 50 ul endpoints closely agree, but its 100 ul onset shifts from 8.23 to 11.62 ml. The newly paired loading difference is only -0.48 ml versus the original -4.00 ml; the small completion difference changes direction. Its sampled 5/1 onset depression remains unreplicated. For H29, m32 identical-input completion changes from 20.07 to 10.98 ml, withdrawing support for a stable 5/1 maximum without identifying either record as erroneous. New m69/m70 curves support shallow onset through 20/1, while m182 shows completion growth before clearer onset growth. H27 is revised: m87 completion at 50 ul is 13.18/13.43/19.70 ml across 2/1, 5/1 and 10/1, so the 150 ul decline does not transfer. Its 50-to-150 ul completion shift diminishes from +10.33 to +4.04 to +2.09 ml. H30 rejects the large predicted m130 transition through 20/1: measured 150 ul endpoints remain only 6.23/13.36 ml there. H31 gains support from m53's controlled joint growth, but observed 6209df8dd01072ab8a47 is m59 and provides no m53 5/1 evidence. H26's predicted pronounced trough is greatly attenuated by m197 completion of 25.00 ml at 2/1, only 0.53 ml below 1/1; a reproducible minimum is unestablished. H28 is refined by completion-dominated m198 growth from 1/1 to 2/1 before its later joint rise, and modest carbonyl-free m201 growth. The m18 extension supports a shallow ordinary ester regime. Earlier m80-transition and m68-rebound expectations remain rejected over measured ranges. Exceptional m177, m120 and m207 inputs remain unreplicated, and the isolated m117 near-reversal is preserved without mechanistic generalization. All residuals discussed are historical premeasurement errors; current candidate records, including the selected repeat, contain predictions only.
batch_rationale: The latest repeats make additional deterministic interpretation of the m75 loading step and m32 completion elevation premature. Acquisition therefore shifts toward connected structural-transfer questions, with one m163 repeat because its substantial current disagreement concerns an already measured complete input. The m162/m163 curves distinguish nitrile response shapes under their respective injection conditions. Three m87 measurements form a two-ratio loading comparison with an observed corner and constrain the strongest remaining completion-loading association. Branched, cyclic and fused ketone measurements test the structural range of early onset. The corrected m53/m59 comparisons repair an important memory attribution error. Ordinary ester curves and two phenolic sequences broaden learning beyond the most intensively investigated conditional surfaces.

possible_model_blind_spots: OBSERVED-BASED INFERENCE: m75 and m32 repeats show that singleton loading minima or completion elevations can be unstable. A deterministic condition surface can overfit them unless repeated-input variation remains visible.
OBSERVED-BASED INFERENCE: historical excessive nitrile growth, insufficient aldehyde growth and excessive fused-ketone onset growth cannot be repaired by one signed polarity or carbonyl correction.

GENERAL CHEMICAL KNOWLEDGE: EA generally strengthens silica elution; increasing PE/EA weakens the mobile phase, and 0/1 is pure EA. Hydrogen bonding and functional-group accessibility can affect adsorption.

UNTESTED HYPOTHESES: adsorption nonlinearity, injection focusing, solubility, integration differences and unrecorded experimental variation could contribute to discrepancies. Endpoints alone do not distinguish them.

choices.reason: Repeat m163 at 50/1, 50 ul, PE 300 ul. Its current prediction disagrees strongly with the observed identical input; repetition tests persistence before interpreting that discrepancy as a stable response.
m163 at 2/1, 50 ul starts a controlled connection between its measured pure-EA baseline and repeated 50/1 input, locating the lower-ratio nitrile response.
m163 at 10/1, 50 ul tests whether appreciable joint growth occurs at an intermediate ratio after m130's large predicted rise failed.
m163 at 20/1, 50 ul connects the selected intermediate ratios to its repeated 50/1 boundary, distinguishing gradual growth from a localized response change.
m162 at 2/1, 50 ul extends its measured pure-EA baseline and anchors a second controlled aryl-nitrile curve under DCM loading.
m162 at 5/1, 50 ul locates curvature between selected 2/1 and 10/1, testing when growth begins toward its measured larger 50/1 endpoints.
m162 at 10/1, 50 ul completes the intermediate sequence. Comparison with m163 retains their different loading solvents and masses rather than isolating a halogen effect.
m87 at 2/1, 100 ul interpolates the substantial completion difference between measured 50 and 150 ul while testing whether onset remains comparatively insensitive.
m87 at 20/1, 50 ul connects measured 10/1 and 50/1 at identical loading and establishes the higher-ratio side of a loading comparison.
m87 at 20/1, 100 ul pairs with selected 50 ul. Together with the 2/1 anchors, it tests whether completion loading sensitivity remains attenuated during later ratio growth.
Branched aryl ketone m54 at 2/1, 100 ul bridges its measured 50 ul input and anchors a controlled comparison with the shallow-onset m69/m70 curves.
m54 at 10/1, 100 ul measures the intermediate response of a branched carbonyl substituent, testing whether onset stays early independently of completion.
m54 at 20/1, 100 ul completes the matched extension and tests the structural range of shallow onset after the longer linear alkyl ketones remained early through 20/1.
Cyclohexyl phenyl ketone m175 at 5/1, 100 ul extends its measured 2/1 anchor, testing cyclic-versus-linear carbonyl-substituent transfer.
m175 at 10/1, 100 ul completes the local ratio sequence and tests the predicted nearly unchanged completion from 5/1 while onset remains early.
m182 at 2/1, 100 ul fills the gap between measured 1/1 and 5/1. It tests a predicted local onset elevation despite early onset at both measured neighbors.
Actual m59 at 2/1, 50 ul supplies a lower-ratio comparison to its measured 5/1 input, testing a flexible ether-containing aldehyde under fixed DCM loading.
m59 at 10/1, 50 ul completes the controlled sequence through its actual 5/1 anchor, distinguishing strong onset growth from a completion-dominated response.
Actual m53 at 2/1, 50 ul creates a genuine lower-loading contrast to measured 100 ul after correcting the false m59-to-m53 anchor attribution.
m53 at 10/1, 50 ul pairs with selected 2/1 and directly contrasts with measured 100 ul, testing loading transfer of its established joint ratio growth.
Cinnamate ester m73 at 2/1, 100 ul extends its measured pure-EA input at the same recorded density and loading, testing predicted earlier completion.
m73 at 10/1, 100 ul completes a controlled sequence from pure EA through 2/1, distinguishing a persistent completion decrease from recovery at ordinary endpoint scale.
Phenylacetate ester m83 at 2/1, 100 ul extends its measured 1/1 baseline and bridges the measured 150 ul input, separating ratio progression from loading.
m83 at 10/1, 100 ul supplies the matched higher-ratio slope, testing ester transfer across carbonyl conjugation and spacing while retaining its PE loading.
Ortho-isopropylphenol m58 at 1/1, 50 ul anchors a phenolic-donor curve connected to its measured 5/1 input, broadening transfer beyond alcohol and hydroxyaldehyde surfaces.
m58 at 2/1, 50 ul tests the lower-ratio shape before its early-onset measured 5/1 input, without assuming that hydroxyl membership imposes a common progression.
m58 at 10/1, 50 ul measures the continuation beyond its measured 5/1 response and locates whether onset begins rising with completion.
m58 at 20/1, 50 ul completes the connected phenolic curve, testing the transition toward larger endpoints under unchanged DCM loading.
Trifluoromethoxyphenol m209 at 1/1, 100 ul bridges its measured 50 ul baseline and establishes the loading context for a controlled ratio sequence.
m209 at 2/1, 100 ul measures its first controlled ratio increment, separating an early molecular offset from the larger response represented by its measured 20/1, 50 ul input.
m209 at 5/1, 100 ul locates intermediate growth in the fixed-loading phenolic curve and tests whether onset and completion begin changing together.
m209 at 10/1, 100 ul completes the controlled extension. Comparison with m58 tests differentiated phenolic responses while preserving substitution, mass and loading-solvent differences.

hypotheses.content: The earlier interpretation of a reproducible m75 10/1 onset loading step is weakened. The 50 ul input repeats closely, but the 100 ul onset changes substantially. The sampled 5/1, 50 ul onset depression and the 2/1 loading association remain unreplicated.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Unstable differences should not become strong deterministic loading interactions during retraining.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Would further balanced identical-input repeats establish a persistent loading difference? This batch assigns that question lower priority after the latest evidence.

hypotheses.content: m87 has a completion-specific loading association that diminishes across the sampled ratios. The 150 ul completion decline from 2/1 to 5/1 does not transfer to 50 ul. Its midpoint loading shape and later-ratio loading sensitivity remain unresolved.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The model needs conditional completion responses rather than a molecular offset or shared onset/completion loading correction.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does 100 ul interpolate the 2/1 completion bracket, and is the 50-to-100 ul completion difference smaller at 20/1?

hypotheses.content: Ketone onset and completion slopes depend on carbonyl environment. m69/m70 retain early onset through 20/1, while m182 develops clearer onset growth after completion has already increased. The paired m32 measurements withdraw support for a stable 5/1 completion maximum.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Branched and cyclic substituent curves test structural limits of shallow-onset transfer, and the m182 interior point tests a localized onset prediction.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do m54 and m175 retain shallow onset over their controlled extensions, and does m182 remain early at 2/1 between its measured neighbors?

hypotheses.content: Aryl nitriles require differentiated response curves. The large forecast m130 transition is rejected through 20/1, m144 has a modest later rise, and m162's larger measured 50/1 endpoints leave its intermediate growth location unknown.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: A connected m162 curve tests transfer after excessive historical nitrile ratio sensitivity without moving the failed m130 transition to another boundary.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At fixed 50 ul, does m162 grow gradually across 2/1, 5/1 and 10/1 or remain shallow before its measured 50/1 response?

hypotheses.content: m53 exhibits joint ratio growth at 100 ul, but lower-loading transfer remains unmeasured. Its purported 5/1 anchor belongs to m59, whose distinct flexible ether-containing aldehyde environment has its own sparse response evidence.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Correctly aligned curves distinguish loading transfer from structural response and prevent decisions based on a nonexistent m53 observation.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m53 preserve its 2/1-to-10/1 growth at 50 ul, and how does actual m59 progress around its measured 5/1 input at that loading?

hypotheses.content: Conjugated cinnamate m73 and alkyl-spaced phenylacetate m83 may have different endpoint slopes. The long measured pure-EA completion of m73 does not establish an intermediate-ratio decline; m83's existing anchors also leave a loading mismatch.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Two ordinary ester curves constrain response shape and structural transfer at modest endpoint scales, where narrow prediction widths supply no acquisition guarantee.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At fixed 100 ul, does m73 completion decrease from pure EA and then recover, while m83 grows from its measured 1/1 baseline?

hypotheses.content: Phenolic donors need not inherit the ratio slopes of aliphatic alcohols or hydroxyaldehydes. m58 retains early onset at measured 5/1 inputs, while m209 has substantially larger measured 20/1 endpoints. Their transition locations remain incompletely sampled under matched loading.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Connected phenolic curves extend donor-environment representation and test onset/completion coupling outside densely investigated alcohol surfaces.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Where does m58 begin growing beyond 5/1, and how does m209 progress from 1/1 through 10/1 at fixed 100 ul?

hypotheses.content: At the already measured m163 50/1, 50 ul input, the current model predicts both endpoints substantially later than the recorded measurement. A persistent fit discrepancy and repeated-input variation remain competing explanations; its intermediate curve is sparsely constrained.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: One repeat tests persistence, while connected intermediate labels can constrain response shape. Repetition alone cannot diagnose the fitting or data-handling cause.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does the identical 50/1 input again give early onset and moderate completion, and how do 2/1, 10/1 and 20/1 approach that endpoint?

selected_plan.batch_rationale: The latest repeats make additional deterministic interpretation of the m75 loading step and m32 completion elevation premature. Acquisition therefore shifts toward connected structural-transfer questions, with one m163 repeat because its substantial current disagreement concerns an already measured complete input. The m162/m163 curves distinguish nitrile response shapes under their respective injection conditions. Three m87 measurements form a two-ratio loading comparison with an observed corner and constrain the strongest remaining completion-loading association. Branched, cyclic and fused ketone measurements test the structural range of early onset. The corrected m53/m59 comparisons repair an important memory attribution error. Ordinary ester curves and two phenolic sequences broaden learning beyond the most intensively investigated conditional surfaces.
selected_plan.expected_learning_value: Expected benefits are improved separation of molecular offsets, ratio slopes and endpoint-specific loading effects across 12 identities. The nitrile measurements can limit excessive transfer of joint growth; the m87 comparison can teach completion interactions with comparatively stable onset. Ketone, aldehyde, ester and phenolic curves provide interpretable transfer evidence, including useful local invariance if changes are small. The m163 repeat can clarify label persistence but cannot by itself fix a training-fit problem. No supplied evidence supports a numerical estimate of retrained overall Row accuracy gain.
selected_plan.feedback_interpretation: The authoritative state is 813 observed records and 2,517 candidates. H15 is weakened: m75's repeated 50 ul endpoints closely agree, but its 100 ul onset shifts from 8.23 to 11.62 ml. The newly paired loading difference is only -0.48 ml versus the original -4.00 ml; the small completion difference changes direction. Its sampled 5/1 onset depression remains unreplicated. For H29, m32 identical-input completion changes from 20.07 to 10.98 ml, withdrawing support for a stable 5/1 maximum without identifying either record as erroneous. New m69/m70 curves support shallow onset through 20/1, while m182 shows completion growth before clearer onset growth. H27 is revised: m87 completion at 50 ul is 13.18/13.43/19.70 ml across 2/1, 5/1 and 10/1, so the 150 ul decline does not transfer. Its 50-to-150 ul completion shift diminishes from +10.33 to +4.04 to +2.09 ml. H30 rejects the large predicted m130 transition through 20/1: measured 150 ul endpoints remain only 6.23/13.36 ml there. H31 gains support from m53's controlled joint growth, but observed 6209df8dd01072ab8a47 is m59 and provides no m53 5/1 evidence. H26's predicted pronounced trough is greatly attenuated by m197 completion of 25.00 ml at 2/1, only 0.53 ml below 1/1; a reproducible minimum is unestablished. H28 is refined by completion-dominated m198 growth from 1/1 to 2/1 before its later joint rise, and modest carbonyl-free m201 growth. The m18 extension supports a shallow ordinary ester regime. Earlier m80-transition and m68-rebound expectations remain rejected over measured ranges. Exceptional m177, m120 and m207 inputs remain unreplicated, and the isolated m117 near-reversal is preserved without mechanistic generalization. All residuals discussed are historical premeasurement errors; current candidate records, including the selected repeat, contain predictions only.
